Step: Feet on the floor. Sit up on the edge of the bed for 10 seconds
Water — a full glass, before anything else
Meds, if you take them. Same place, every day, visible
Open the curtains / get light on your face
Open your Desk → tap today's energy (one tap)
Read your One Thing. Don't do it. Just read it
Eat something. Anything. A low bar on purpose
Stop. Routine complete
Clear the desk surface. Everything off it, into one pile if necessary
Water within reach
Phone in a drawer or another room
Open your Desk. Tap energy
Pick the One Thing for today — match it to the energy you just logged
Write its first physical action (open what? click what?)
Timer: 25 minutes. Start the first physical action
Brain dump everything still in your head. Fragments only
Write tomorrow's One Thing and its first physical action
Any promise you made today that isn't written down → write it down now
Close the tabs. All of them. They are not a to-do list
Tidy the desk surface — 60 seconds, not properly
Say out loud: "Work is finished for today."
Kitchen: everything into the sink or the dishwasher. Not washed — collected
One surface cleared. Any surface
Tomorrow's launch kit by the door: keys, bag, anything you must not forget
Charge your phone outside the bedroom if you can
Set the alarm. And a leaving alarm if you have to be somewhere
Meds in place for the morning, where you'll see them
Stop. The day's over and nothing else is required of you
Touch each one and say it: phone, keys, wallet
Today's extras: meds, laptop, charger, the document, the gift
Check the address in the actual booking, not from memory
Leave. Don't start anything. Not one small thing
Before you do anything else, open the Brain Dump
What did I agree to do? Dump each one, no formatting
What did someone else agree to do? Dump it — nobody else will remember
Any date mentioned → straight into the calendar now
Stop. Triage later, not now
Water. Food. Both, now, before any thinking
Meds if you take them and haven't
Open Bad Day Mode — not your task list
Do one thing from it. Under two minutes. One
Tell one person, or post in #low-energy-days. A single emoji counts
Stop. Today is complete
Timer: 15 minutes. Music on
Four containers: bin bag, elsewhere bag, LATER box, the surface
One item at a time. Two seconds per item. Four destinations, no fifth
Holding something and thinking about it? → LATER box, immediately
Timer goes → stop, even mid-pile
Bin bag to the actual bin. The only step you must finish
LATER box into a cupboard with a date 30 days out
Select everything older than 30 days → folder OLD. Not deleted
Timer: 6 minutes on what's left. REPLY / task written down / archive
Unsubscribe from the next five marketing emails you see
Stop. Replies are a separate job for a separate day
Night before: confirm time and address from the actual booking
Travel time × 1.5 → set a leaving alarm
Write the three things you need to say or ask. Most important first
By the door: ID, reference number, payment method, water
On the day: alarm goes → leave within 10 minutes, start nothing
Before leaving, ask: "What happens next, and who does it?" Write the answer down there and then
Calendar, next 7 days only. Count the fixed commitments. Say the number out loud
Spot anything you'd forgotten → that was the dread
Name the one hard thing of the week, in writing, and pick its day
Cancel one thing. There's usually one. Use script S3
Write what you're not doing this week — explicitly
Monday's One Thing + its first physical action
Clothes out, bag packed, both alarms set
Put one nice thing in the week, on a specific day
Laptop shut. No "quick look" at email
Don't read your task list. Not yet
Open the Frozen view. Delete ten things. Deleting is doing
Open Real Deadlines. Is anything actually on fire? Usually no
Pick one 15-minute task → make it The One Thing
Do it, or don't. Either way, re-entry is complete
Say hi in #re-entry if you feel like it. Or don't
